title: D2C: a ChatGPT plugin that draws diagrams

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Remember when ChatGPT plugins were a thing? Antoine built one that turned a conversation into a diagram.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I do remember. What did it draw?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Diagrams written in PlantUML or Mermaid. You describe a system in the chat, and the plugin generates the diagram from it. It's called D2COpenAIPlugin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And it was a proper plugin, not a script on the side?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A proper ChatGPT plugin, with a diagram-oriented interface. The page is clear that it's a historical project, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's a Python app built on FastAPI. The original setup was Python, a virtual environment through poetry, installing the dependencies, and starting a local server on port fifty-three oh three.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the instructions might be out of date.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the caveat. The page labels them as the original plugin environment, and the manifest and configuration stay in the source repository.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where would someone look for more?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The project documentation covers the implementation and API routes, and the GitHub repository has the original code. It's worth reading as an early example of diagrams-from-chat, the idea behind Antoine's later diagram work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The written page has the links.
